newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria awards grain tenders to Glencore, Nada.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria awards grain tenders to Glencore, Nada.

text.p: Swiss firm Glencore and Bulgaria's Nada will import 100,000 tonnes of wheat against forward contracts to export 134,000 tonnes from the new crop, Bulgaria's agriculture minister said on Thursday.
Roumen Hristov said the ministry would sign contracts with the two firms, chosen out of a total of eight bidders.
Glencore would import 50,000 tonnes against receiving 68,000 tonnes of wheat from the new crop and Nada would import the same quantity against 66,000 tones of exports from the new crop.
The contracts would be sealed after the two firms presented banking guarantees, Hristov told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
Bulgaria's Bulbank would give a banking guarantee to Glencore, and Nada should win a guarantee by a bank in which the state holds a stake bigger than 50 percent, he added.
"Other contracts for wheat imports against quantities from the new crop will not be sealed as Bulgaria cannot afford bigger exports than those which have already been agreed," Hristov said.

He said 100,000 tonnes of wheat should be exported to Poland in exchange for the same amount of immediate imports from there agreed during a visit by President Petar Stoyanov last week, although there could be other methods of payment.
Another 35,000 tonnes from the new crop would be bartered for combine harvesters, he said.

Hristov is due to leave for Germany on Monday to negotiate the opening of a 100 million mark credit line for imports of agricultural machinery and equipment against Bulgarian products, including vegetables and fruit but not wine.
Officials have said Bulgaria needed 450,000 tonnes of wheat to fill the gap until the new crop comes in.
Deputy Agriculture Minister Alexander Rangelov said Sofia's mill had sealed a deal with Argentina for 130,000 tonnes of grain and would receive the first 31,000 tonnes in March.
Bulgaria is also negotiating an agreement under the U.S. Department of Agriculture's GSM-102 export credit guarantee programme for 130,000-150,000 tonnes of grain supplies.
The European Union is expected to provide grain aid to Bulgaria worth about two million Ecus.

Bulgaria is battling an acute grain shortage after uncontrolled exports two years ago depleted supplies. A poor harvest last year was attributed to bad weather and a lack of cash for fertilisers. -- Roumiana Tiholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
